page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated virtual CPUs, mapped from 32 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.3 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The processor configuration includes a 45 MB L3 cache, 32 KB L1d cache, and 0.25 MB L2 cache. The instance is equipped with 240 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results indicate a distinct performance profile characterized by weak single-core capabilities and average multi-core throughput. Single-core tests, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression/decompression, consistently rank in the bottom 25%. However, the 64-vCPU allocation elevates multi-core performance to average levels, as demonstrated by Geekbench multi-core, Passmark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scores. Memory bandwidth remains average across both cached small-block and uncached large-block read/write operations.

For application workloads, the instance delivers average throughput for Redis SET operations, static web serving, and LLM prompt processing across small, medium, and large models. Conversely, LLM text generation speeds are weak, falling into the bottom 25% due to single-thread and memory-bound constraints. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-64 offers a balanced resource allocation for legacy multi-threaded workloads, but the older Intel Xeon architecture presents a performance-per-resource tradeoff compared to newer hardware generations. It is suitable for multi-threaded web serving, database operations, and general-purpose enterprise applications that scale across many cores but do not require high single-thread performance.
